newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG RETAIN TWO-POINT ADVANTAGE OVER BASTIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG RETAIN TWO-POINT ADVANTAGE OVER BASTIA.

text.p: Paris St Germain stayed on course for France's second berth in next season's European Champions' League by holding Bastia to a 1-1 draw in the French first division on Tuesday.
The draw also edged leaders Monaco, 11 points in front of PSG before their visit to Bordeaux on Wednesday, nearer their sixth league championship.
Monaco have 68 points, second-placed PSG 57 and Bastia, who are third, 55.

French international Patrice Loko put PSG ahead with a counter-attack after 14 minutes, beating the offside trap to take a through ball from Bernard Allou and slot it past Bastia keeper Fabien Piveteau.
The Corsican side had more of the ball and made it count when they equalised 10 minutes later through Slovakian Lubomir Moravcik.
The midfielder scored with a 25-metre free kick which flew past French international goalkeeper Bernard Lama and into the top left hand corner.
Lama twice foiled Bastia's Slovenian striker Ermin Siljak later in the first half to keep PSG in the game.
Wilfried Siljak was standing in for Bastia's top striker Anton Drobnjak. The 16-goal Yugoslav missed the match after his mother's death on Tuesday morning.
